description:
FILED s467 (Fable, 2026-09-04), found while verifying README claims.

`./pl2cl --executable -o BIN prog.pl` prints "Created: BIN" and writes a 48 MB executable, but:
  - the PROGRAM RUNS DURING THE BUILD: its stdout appears in the build output, and a file it opens for writing exists after the build;
  - the produced BIN runs, exits 0, and does NOTHING: no stdout, no stderr, the marker file is not created.
Probe: scratchpad readme/exe.pl (prints to stdout/stderr, writes a marker file); build, `ls marker` -> present; rm; run BIN -> rc 0, empty stdout+stderr, no marker.

`--bundle -o X.fasl` produces a 2.2 MB fasl (not verified whether LOADING it runs the program or whether the program also ran at build time).

Cause (not verified; the obvious reading of pl2cl's `do_bundle`): the program's top-level forms are LOADED into the image before `save-lisp-and-die`, so they execute at build time, and the saved toplevel does not re-run them (or has no :toplevel that runs the program).  The `pcl --help` text already says standalone compilation "is not supported yet (planned, Phase 6)"; pl2cl's header advertises both flags without that caveat.

Options: (a) make it real -- save the image with a :toplevel function that runs the program's main forms at start (the forms must be compiled into a function rather than loaded at build), plus @ARGV/%ENV/$0 taken at run time, exit code propagated; or (b) until (a), make the two flags DIE with the pcl --help sentence rather than produce a binary that silently does nothing (rule 12: a missing case dies).  (b) is a one-line filler; (a) is docs/single-binary-plan.md (#756).

README (s467) does not mention the flags.

=== DONE (s473i) ===
SHIPPED 2026-09-08 as option (a) â it is REAL, not a refusal.

MEASURED FIRST, and it was worse than filed: with an `exit` anywhere in the
program the program's exit killed the BUILD sbcl, so no binary was written at
all ("Failed to create executable (sbcl exit code: 768)").  Without an `exit`,
the marker file existed after the BUILD and the 49 MB binary exited 0 in
silence, exactly as filed.

NO NEW EMISSION MODE WAS NEEDED â the plan's `--build-mode` split already
exists in the output.  Pl/Parser2.pm 2044-2135 (the #456(b)/#469 phase model)
assembles every section's COMPILE phase, then emits exactly ONE
`(p-run-compile-phase-blocks)`, then every section's RUN phase.  Measured:
111/111 perl-tests transpiles have exactly one, at column 0, and the run part
contains no defvar / p-sub / p-defcell.  So the split is a READ of the emitted
file.

cl/pcl-build-exe.lisp (new; loaded only by the build sbcl, but its toplevel
function is saved into the image):
  * %p-exe-load-program reads form by form, EVALuating the compile phase as it
    goes (read and eval must interleave: `(p-defpackage :main)` has to have run
    before `(in-package :main)` can be READ) and collecting the run phase;
    an `in-package` past the boundary is reader state, never a thunk; no
    boundary at all is a hard error, never a fall-through.
  * %p-exe-compile-run-phase compiles ONE thunk per top-level form (`load`'s
    own granularity) inside a with-compilation-unit.
  * %p-exe-toplevel sets @ARGV/$0 from sb-ext:*posix-argv*, runs the thunks,
    exits 0; an uncaught error prints the message and nothing else and exits
    255 (PCL_BACKTRACE=1 adds the CL backtrace).  :save-runtime-options t so
    the binary does not eat its own arguments.

pl2cl: `do_executable` replaces the old `load`-then-save; both build modes now
start from PCLSbcl's prefix (the cached core), so the binary carries the same
runtime `pcl` runs and the build stops recompiling the runtime.  `--bundle`
had the SAME build-time run (it `--load`ed the bundle "to get ASDF/cl-ppcre"
before compile-file) and now loads only the runtime.

MEASURED vs perl on the same source: exit 3 -> rc 3, stdout BYTE-IDENTICAL,
END blocks run, marker written at RUN time and not at build (BEGIN-RAN appears
on the BUILD's stderr, which is what "build = perl's compile phase" means);
uncaught die -> rc 255, stderr = the message alone (`pcl` itself still prints
an SBCL backtrace and exits 1); `use List::Util` + an OO package + sprintf +
s/// + %ENV + $$ -> identical, and it runs under `env -i` from another cwd.
Build 3.2 s -> 0.9 s (--executable), 7.2 s -> 4.4 s (--bundle).

STILL NOT STANDALONE, documented rather than assumed (single-binary-plan steps
3-5, #217): strace shows the binary opening cl/pcl-pack.lisp from the BUILD
TREE at run time, and a `require` that misses the module cache still shells
out to perl+pl2cl.  Said in `pl2cl --help`, `pcl --help`, README, CHANGELOG.

Guards: tools/t/executable-01.t (24 rows, ~8 s wall, NOT in the gate; 17 of 24
FAIL on the a9f2a264 extraction) + 2 help-text rows in Pl/t/cache-surface-01.t
(50 -> 52; both fail on the extraction).
subject: `pl2cl --executable` runs the PROGRAM AT BUILD TIME and produces a 48 MB binary that does nothing (exit 0, no output); `--bundle` unverified -- make it real (#756's plan) or make both flags die until then
